2	
3	## Overview
4	Four global ocean health indicators tracked biennially from 1990 to 2014 and annually from 2015 to 2024, each with distinct units and trend directions, designed to illustrate the compound stress on marine ecosystems.
5	
6	## Data Source
7	
8	### sea_surface_temperature_anomaly
9	- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `anomaly_c` (float, °C relative to 1961–1990 baseline)
10	- **Range**: 0.04 to 0.91 °C
11	- **Trend**: Generally increasing with interannual variability; sharp rise post-2022
12	
13	### ocean_ph
14	- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `ph` (float, dimensionless pH scale)
15	- **Range**: 8.034 to 8.110
16	- **Trend**: Steady decline (increasing acidity); narrow numerical range requiring fine-scale axis
17	
18	### coral_cover
19	- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `cover_pct` (float, percentage of reef area)
20	- **Range**: 11.5% to 33.5%
21	- **Trend**: Long-term decline with a notable drop during the 1998 bleaching event and accelerating loss after 2015
22	
23	### ocean_plastic_pollution
24	- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `plastic_mmt` (float, million metric tons cumulative)
25	- **Range**: 25 to 255 million metric tons
26	- **Trend**: Near-exponential growth throughout the period
27	
28	## Data Notes
29	- Temperature anomalies are modeled global means; regional values vary significantly.
30	- Ocean pH values represent open-ocean surface averages; coastal and deep-water pH differ.
31	- Coral cover estimates are synthesized from GCRMN-style monitoring and carry ±2–4% uncertainty.
32	- Plastic pollution figures are cumulative stock estimates and include modeled seafloor accumulation, which is the largest and most uncertain component.

# Ocean Health Multi-Indicator Time Series (1990–2024)

## Overview
Four global ocean health indicators tracked biennially from 1990 to 2014 and annually from 2015 to 2024, each with distinct units and trend directions, designed to illustrate the compound stress on marine ecosystems.

## Data Source

### sea_surface_temperature_anomaly
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `anomaly_c` (float, °C relative to 1961–1990 baseline)
- **Range**: 0.04 to 0.91 °C
- **Trend**: Generally increasing with interannual variability; sharp rise post-2022

### ocean_ph
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `ph` (float, dimensionless pH scale)
- **Range**: 8.034 to 8.110
- **Trend**: Steady decline (increasing acidity); narrow numerical range requiring fine-scale axis

### coral_cover
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `cover_pct` (float, percentage of reef area)
- **Range**: 11.5% to 33.5%
- **Trend**: Long-term decline with a notable drop during the 1998 bleaching event and accelerating loss after 2015

### ocean_plastic_pollution

# Ocean Health Multi-Indicator Time Series (1990–2024)

## Overview
Four global ocean health indicators tracked biennially from 1990 to 2014 and annually from 2015 to 2024, each with distinct units and trend directions, designed to illustrate the compound stress on marine ecosystems.

## Data Source

### sea_surface_temperature_anomaly
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `anomaly_c` (float, °C relative to 1961–1990 baseline)
- **Range**: 0.04 to 0.91 °C
- **Trend**: Generally increasing with interannual variability; sharp rise post-2022

### ocean_ph
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `ph` (float, dimensionless pH scale)
- **Range**: 8.034 to 8.110
- **Trend**: Steady decline (increasing acidity); narrow numerical range requiring fine-scale axis

### coral_cover
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `cover_pct` (float, percentage of reef area)
- **Range**: 11.5% to 33.5%
- **Trend**: Long-term decline with a notable drop during the 1998 bleaching event and accelerating loss after 2015

### ocean_plastic_pollution
- **Fields**: `year` (integer, 1990–2024), `plastic_mmt` (float, million metric tons cumulative)
- **Range**: 25 to 255 million metric tons
- **Trend**: Near-exponential growth throughout the period

## Data Notes
- Temperature anomalies are modeled global means; regional values vary significantly.
- Ocean pH values represent open-ocean surface averages; coastal and deep-water pH differ.
- Coral cover estimates are synthesized from GCRMN-style monitoring and carry ±2–4% uncertainty.
- Plastic pollution figures are cumulative stock estimates and include modeled seafloor accumulation, which is the largest and most uncertain component.

Skip to content
Ocean Health Synthesis · 1990–2024

Multi-Indicator Ocean Health Deterioration

Four concurrent stressors — rising temperatures, increasing acidity, collapsing coral cover, and surging plastic accumulation — document compound ecosystem decline over three decades.

SST Anomaly
+0.91°C
2024 vs 1961–1990 baseline · ↑ from +0.12°C in 1990
Ocean pH
8.034
2024 · ↓ −0.076 units since 1990
Coral Cover
11.5%
2024 · ↓ from 33.5% in 1990 (−66%)
Plastic Pollution
255 MMT
2024 cumulative · ↑ 10× since 1990

Coral Collapse Acceleration

Coral cover declined from 22.6% in 2015 to 11.5% by 2024 — a loss of nearly half of remaining reefs in just 9 years, more than double the rate of the preceding decade.

Unprecedented Warming

SST anomaly surged from +0.62°C (2016) to +0.91°C (2024), with the most recent 4 years exceeding all prior records and driving coral bleaching events globally.

Exponential Plastic Growth

Ocean plastic accumulation follows a near-exponential trajectory, growing from 25 MMT (1990) to 255 MMT (2024) — growing faster per decade than all other indicators combined.

Acidification Steady Decline

Ocean pH has dropped 0.076 units since 1990 — representing a ~19% increase in hydrogen ion concentration, steadily compressing the viable chemistry window for calcifying organisms.

Simultaneous Multi-Indicator Trends, 1990–2024

Four independent y-axes enable direct trend-shape comparison across indicators with incompatible units. Contrasting directions — rising temperature and plastic, falling pH and coral cover — illustrate the convergent pressure on marine ecosystems.

1998 El Niño bleaching event
2015–16 record SST spike
Post-2015 coral collapse acceleration
2023–24 unprecedented warming

Indicator Reference

Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly (°C)
Annual global mean SST departure from 1961–1990 baseline. Left y-axis (0 to 1.0°C). Solid line.
Ocean pH (dimensionless)
Annual mean surface ocean pH. Second y-axis (8.02–8.12). Dashed line. Declining = increasing acidity.
Coral Cover (% of reef area)
Global average hard coral cover from monitoring networks. Third y-axis (0–40%). Dotted line.
Ocean Plastic Pollution (MMT)
Cumulative plastic mass including seafloor. Right y-axis (0–280 MMT). Dash-dot line. Near-exponential curve.
Data Notes: Temperature anomalies are modelled global means; regional values vary significantly. Ocean pH values represent open-ocean surface averages. Coral cover estimates carry ±2–4% uncertainty. Plastic pollution figures are cumulative stock estimates including modelled seafloor accumulation. Biennial sampling 1990–2014; annual from 2015. All data sourced from source_data.json.
